One is cheaper to start, the other builds deeper pipelines. Here's which fits your team in 2026. Artisan's AI SDR Ava starts at roughly $1,500/month; 11x's Alice runs closer to $5,000 for comparable outreach volume. Artisan is a more affordable AI BDR platform with a built-in contact database and multi-channel outreach, but its personalization doesn't hold up for technical products, LinkedIn automation carries real account-ban risk, and neither vendor publishes pricing publicly. The strongest Artisan alternatives in 2026 are 11x for enterprise-scale sequences, Clay for full workflow control, and Smartlead for deliverability-first teams. By Rishabh Ambasta , Founder, Modern Inbound. TL;DR Cheapest to start: Artisan (approx. $1,500/mo vs. $5,000+ for 11x, per vendor sales calls) Best for enterprise: 11x (dual AI agents, deeper CRM sync, higher volume) Best for SMB or early-stage: Artisan (lower entry cost, faster to launch) Most transparent pricing: Neither. Both require a discovery call to get a quote. Side-by-Side Comparison Artisan and 11x are the two most-funded AI SDR platforms available today, but they're built for different buyers. Artisan targets early-stage teams who want one tool to replace a BDR hire. 11x targets mature sales orgs that already run structured sequences and need AI handling the execution layer on top of an existing process. Tool Starting Price Best For Standout Feature Artisan ~$1,500/mo SMB outbound teams All-in-one AI BDR with 300M+ contact database, per Artisan's product page 11x ~$5,000/mo Enterprise outbound Dual AI agents: Alice for outbound, Jordan for inbound, per 11x's product page Clay $149/mo Custom AI enrichment workflows Waterfall enrichment across 75+ data providers, per Clay's pricing page Smartlead $39/mo High-volume cold email Unlimited mailboxes with built-in warm-up at base tier, per Smartlead's pricing page Instantly $37/mo Cold email at scale AI-optimized send scheduling with deliverability network, per Instantly's site What Artisan Actually Does Artisan is a venture-backed AI BDR platform that sells Ava, an AI agent who finds leads, writes personalized emails, and sends LinkedIn messages on autopilot. It's the fastest way to launch an outbound motion without hiring, but it's not a substitute for a human with real domain expertise in your niche. Personalization quality drops sharply past the first two sequence steps for technical or complex products. Artisan's contact database claims 300M+ profiles, per Artisan's product page. Its autopilot mode runs full campaigns with minimal daily input. That sounds like a win until you realize minimal input also means minimal quality control. Teams selling $20K+ ACV products consistently report on G2 that Ava's messaging reads generic after the first touch. The LinkedIn automation is the bigger risk. Artisan drives Ava's LinkedIn actions through your personal account. LinkedIn's terms of service prohibit third-party automation, and account flags are a real outcome for heavy users, per LinkedIn's platform policy. What 11x Actually Does 11x is an enterprise-focused AI sales platform with two distinct agents: Alice handles outbound prospecting and Jordan handles inbound lead follow-up. It's built for teams with an existing sales process, a defined ICP, and the budget to support premium AI infrastructure. Don't buy 11x as your first outbound experiment. It won't perform if you don't already know what a good sequence looks like. Where 11x outperforms Artisan is in CRM depth and inbound coverage. Alice pulls live CRM data to skip existing customers or recently churned accounts automatically, per 11x's product documentation.
